# A ball with a two-limb center as one with a one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_narrow_2_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$. A ball may also be the whole line or the empty set.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x : x \in X \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c$ and radius $r$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ is a finite ball, and $\lvert x - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c\rvert \le r$.
- **B4.** If $X$ is a finite ball and $\lvert \lvert c\rvert + r\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 2}$, then $Z$ is a finite ball. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 2}$ is $2^{1022}$ for `double`, $2^{126}$ for `float`.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_narrow_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_narrow_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the leading limb, and the radius widened by the second limb (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_narrow_2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_narrow_2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`radd`](radd.md).

```
# A ball with a 2-limb center as a ball with a one-limb center that contains it: the leading limb
# for the center, and the radius plus the magnitude of the second limb, rounded up by radd
# (whose operands are nonnegative here by construction: a radius, and an absolute value). The
# special states pass through: the empty ball (all NaN) gives NaN for the center and the radius;
# the whole line (0, 0, +inf) gives (0, +inf); and a radius that overflows gives the whole line,
# its center replaced by zero, so that the ball is canonical. Bounded when no member exceeds a
# quarter of the overflow threshold: then r + |c1| is below it and radd's result is finite.

a  = abs(c1)
rz = radd(r, a)
wh = eq(rz, const inf)
cz = select(wh, 0, c0)
```
